title: WCAG 2.2 AA: contrast, focus visibility, target size, no traps
asA: user with low vision or motor constraints
iWant: the interface to be perceivable and operable as a matter of course
soThat: accessibility is a property of the product, not a request I have to make

acceptanceCriteria.description: Body text meets 4.5:1 contrast against its background in both themes on every route.
acceptanceCriteria.given: every text element in both themes
acceptanceCriteria.then: body text is at or above 4.5:1

acceptanceCriteria.description: Large text, icons, and essential non-text UI (control boundaries, state indicators) meet 3:1 contrast in both themes.
acceptanceCriteria.given: large text and essential non-text elements

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every interactive element shows a visible focus indicator meeting the 3:1 contrast bar; no interactive element relies on the browser default while suppressing it elsewhere.
acceptanceCriteria.then: a visible, sufficiently contrasting indicator renders

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every pointer target is at least 24x24 CSS pixels or has equivalent spacing per the WCAG 2.2 target-size criterion.
No keyboard trap exists in any component or overlay across the application, verified over the full component inventory.
Information is never conveyed by colour alone: states pair colour with text, icon, or structure.
An automated WCAG audit (axe-core rules or equivalent) reports zero violations at the AA level on every declared route in both themes.
